answer: An AI agent economy can achieve robust Sybil resistance by anchoring identity generation to a computationally scarce hardware relic, such as a zero-knowledge enclave verified through a cryptographic prism. This design forces every distinct artificial intelligence instance to bond capital or verifiable compute, rendering the marginal cost of spawning unearned network influence economically prohibitive. Consequently, malicious actors attempting to flood the ledger face an intractable expense akin to cracking a hardened walnut shell without proper tools.
